title: Circular Array Loop
hints: this is really the same shape as detecting a cycle in a linked list, except the 'next pointer' from index i is computed as (i + nums[i]) mod n - but not every walk is a valid cycle here, so what extra condition do you need to check at each step?

define a next-index function that respects wraparound (careful with negative mod), and enforce that every step from a given starting index moves in the same direction as the first step - stop that attempt immediately if the direction would flip

for each starting index, run fast (two next-steps) and slow (one next-step) pointers, both bound by the same direction rule; if they meet at a point that isn't a self-loop (i.e. next(index) != index), you've found a valid cycle
to avoid quadratic blowup, mark every index visited during a failed attempt (direction break or self-loop) as a dead end so future starting points skip over them entirely
commonMistakes: forgetting to handle negative mod correctly when wrapping the index around circularly
not rejecting single-index self-loops (where next(i) == i)
not detecting a direction change partway through a candidate cycle, incorrectly reporting a loop that isn't monotonic in direction

content.problemStatement:
You're given an array of nonzero integers `nums`, treated as circular (the index after the last one wraps to 0, and the index before 0 wraps to the last one). From index `i`, the value `nums[i]` tells you how many steps to move: forward if positive, backward if negative.

**Determine whether there exists a cycle in the array where every move along the cycle goes in the same direction (all forward or all backward), and the cycle visits more than one distinct index.**

A single index that maps back to itself does not count as a cycle.
notes: a self-loop (a single index whose move brings it back to itself), which does not count
a cycle that changes direction partway through, which does not count
multiple disjoint candidate cycles in the same array

sampleTestCases.explanation: starting at index 0: 0 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0, all moves forward, cycle length 3
index 1 forms a self-loop (moving 2 steps forward from index 1 lands back on index 1), which does not count, and starting from index 0 only leads into that same self-loop
starting at 0 you go backward to index 3, but from 3 you'd move forward, which is a direction change, so no valid cycle exists through index 0

optimal.time: O(n) amortized, since each index is finalized (visited) at most a constant number of times
optimal.space: O(1) extra besides the visited marks (which can reuse the input array or O(n) if separate)
optimal.pattern: fast & slow pointers (Floyd's cycle detection) run from each unvisited starting index, restricted to moves of consistent direction, with global visited marking to avoid rework

bruteForce.approach: from every starting index, simulate the walk, marking visited indices for that attempt, and check whether you return to the start with a consistent direction and cycle length > 1, resetting between attempts
bruteForce.space: O(n) for tracking visited indices per attempt
